subject: Re: Follow-up: Integration + Observability hooks for FintechCo
messages:
From: Alex Li <ali@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T15:08:00-08:00
Subject: Integration follow-up + observability questions

Thanks for the call today — good overview. A few follow-ups from our engineering and SRE teams: 

1) Auth: we currently prefer short-lived tokens (OIDC) over long-lived API keys. Can Redwood support OIDC token exchange or will we need to use API keys for SDKs?
2) Routing & fallbacks: we need predictable latency for user-facing flows and cheaper fallbacks for batch jobs. How do we route between variants (gpt-like-8b / gpt-like-8b-quant)?
3) Observability hooks: our SRE asked for trace correlation (X-Trace-Id), per-token latency headers, and a dashboard-ready metrics export (percentile token latency, model selection, cache hit rate).

Can you share a short tech note and any example config we can show the SREs? Also looping in our SRE alias (sre@fintechco.com) for calendar availability next week.

— Alex
Senior PM, FintechCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <ali@fintechco.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechco.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up + observability questions

Alex — thanks, great questions. Quick recap and proposed next steps below. Attaching our integration guide + observability spec for the SREs.

Recap of asks:
- Auth: OIDC support vs API keys
- Routing / fallbacks: latency SLOs + cheaper variants for batch
- Observability: trace correlation, latency breakdown headers, cache hit metrics, dashboard links

Proposed next steps:
1) Ethan to send a short tech note with recommended SDK setup (OIDC exchange flow + API-key fallback) and sample headers.
2) Schedule a 30-min SRE-focused session next Tue/Thu to walk observability hooks and dashboard demos.
3) We'll provide a mutual action plan (MAP) with owner/responsible and an initial config we recommend for staging.

For transparency: our recommended approach is to support OIDC token exchange in front of our SDKs (we call the exchange endpoint to mint short-lived inference tokens). We can also accept API keys while OIDC integration is being validated. Routing is policy-driven (per-route config) — we can pin your user-facing routes to the low-latency pool and configure automatic fallback to a quantized variant for batch.

Ethan — can you add the technical callouts below and share the sample header list? Vivek — any notes on model/quantization recommendations for FintechCo?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-integration-guide.pdf (pdf), observability-hook-spec.md (markdown)

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <ali@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T17:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up + observability questions

Alex / team — technical note as promised (high level):

1) Auth patterns:
- Recommended: OIDC token exchange (FintechCo IdP -> Redwood exchange endpoint -> short-lived inference token). This avoids long-lived secrets in clients.
- Fallback: scoped API keys for server-side only flows. Keys can be rotated via our Console and mapped to teams/projects.
- Required headers for tracing: X-Trace-Id (your inbound trace), X-Client-Request-Id (idempotency), Authorization: Bearer <inference_token>.

2) SDK setup & sample config:
- SDKs support both OIDC and API-key flows. Example config: set routing.policy = {"latency_slo_ms": 150, "preferred_pool": "low-latency", "fallback": "quantized-8b"}.
- Structured output / tool-calling: Redwood SDK can surface function/tool results as structured JSON. We recommend schema validation on the client to guard against model drift.

3) Routing and model variants:
- Per-route pinning: pin production user-facing route to "low-latency" pool (single-model pin). For batch, set policy to prefer "cost-optimized" pool which uses quantized variants.
- Automatic fallback: if low-latency pool is saturated, requests can be retried to a compatible variant with an explicit header: X-RW-Fallback: allowed.

4) Observability hooks (what we provide):
- Response headers: X-RW-Trace-Id, X-RW-Token-Latency-ms, X-RW-Decode-Latency-ms, X-RW-Model => gpt-like-8b-quant
- Metrics export: per-route token_throughput, token_latency_p50/p90/p99, model_selection_count, kv_cache_hit_rate. Exposed to Prometheus and via our Console dashboards.
- Logging fields we emit: request_id, trace_id (if provided), route_id, model_variant, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_latency_ms.

5) Embeddings & rerankers:
- We recommend computing embeddings in a separate batch pipeline (for safety) and using our reranker endpoint for top-k scoring. Reranker accepts precomputed vectors and returns scores with reason scores in structured JSON.

I'll attach a minimal example config and a small cURL/OIDC flow snippet. Happy to walk through live.

— Ethan
Staff SWE, Infra
Redwood Inference

Attachment: observability-hook-spec.md

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <ali@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up + observability questions

Alex — quick model/ops notes from product/solutions: 

- For customer-facing flows with strict latency SLOs, we typically recommend: gpt-like-8b pinned to low-latency pool (INT8 quant if acceptable), with caching at the prefix level for repeated prompts. Expect median token latency improvements of ~30% with prefix caching.
- For document search/rerank: use our embeddings for vector store + the reranker (cheap model) to get better top-K precision before hitting generation.
- Cost: quantized variants are ~3-4x cheaper per token. We'll include cost-estimates in the MAP.

I'll join the SRE session and bring a small dashboard demo built in Console showing X-RW-Token-Latency-ms percentiles and cache hit rate.

— Vivek
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

- For the OIDC exchange, do you have an endpoint pattern we can test in a staging environment?

Also, Tue 11/24 10:00am PT works for our SREs. I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm.
